llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly lists /home/user/Desktop/ and returns has_new_name (party_poster.webp present) and has_old_name (poster_party_night.webp present), covering both filenames needed to distinguish all outcome states.
Metric awards 0.5 for restore (file on Desktop under either name) and an additional 0.5 for clean rename (new name present, old name absent), totalling 1.0 for full task completion.
Initial state (file in Trash, not on Desktop) correctly yields score 0.0, providing negative-control resistance.
Partial credit scheme distinguishes: nothing done (0.0), only restored (0.5), fully restored and renamed (1.0).

Minor semantic gap: evaluator does not explicitly verify the file was removed from Trash (could pass if a new file is independently created on the Desktop), but this is practically acceptable since restoring from Trash is the only realistic path in the given environment.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optionally add a Trash contents check to confirm poster_party_night.webp is no longer in ~/.local/share/Trash/files/, hardening against a scenario where a fresh file is placed on the Desktop without actually restoring from Trash.
